content: Dimethicone is a dermatological agent approved by the FDA for the treatment of diaper dermatitis, cracked skin, and chapped lips. Common adverse reactions include burning, stinging, redness, or irritation. Adult Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications: Dimethicone is used to treat and prevent diaper dermatitis, protect minor skin irritation associated with diaper dermatitis, and shield the skin from wetness. It also temporarily protects and relieves chapped or cracked skin and lips. Directions for Use: Apply as needed. Wet and soiled diapers, garments, and linens should be changed promptly. Cleanse the affected area and allow it to dry before application. Apply the cream liberally as often as necessary with each diaper, garment, or linen change, especially at bedtime or any time when exposure to soiled materials may be prolonged. Off-Label Use: There is limited information regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported use of dimethicone in adult patients. Contraindications There is limited information regarding contraindications for dimethicone in the drug label. Warnings For external use only. Avoid contact with eyes. Discontinue use and consult a doctor if the condition worsens, symptoms persist for more than 7 days, or symptoms clear up and recur within a few days. Do not use on deep or puncture wounds, animal bites, or serious burns. Keep out of reach of children. If swallowed, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately.
